overview: White plays 3.Bg5 against the Owen, hitting the e7 pawn and aiming at the queen, but leaves e4 undefended. After 3...Bxe4 Black wins a pawn and White has Nc3 and Bxe7 ideas only. The line is a rare surprise weapon.

white_ideas.idea: Use the g5 bishop to harass the queen side with Nc3 and Bxe7 tricks

black_ideas.idea: Take the pawn with ...Bxe4 and return it only if needed
Develop ...f6 or ...h6 to kick the bishop

typical_structures.structure: White d4 centre against a b7 bishop

character.notes: The e4 pawn is offered, so play is tactical.

gambit.notes: 3.Bg5 Bxe4 leaves Black a pawn up.

soundness.notes: Considered dubious; Black has simple answers like ...Bxe4 and ...h6.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3...f6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 b6 2. d4 Bb7 3. Bg5 f6

character.reason: A pawn offer and quick piece play lead to tactical positions.

gambit.reason: White leaves e4 hanging and Black can keep the pawn.

soundness.reason: Black has simple ways to refute the idea.

structure.reason: The centre opens for the pieces after the e4 capture.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose 3.Bg5 against the Owen.

level.reason: A dubious gambit is never Beginner.

plans.reason: White hopes to use time lost by Black.
